skills.name: Writing a talk for an audience

note.text: A written talk is meant to be heard by a particular audience. A greeting can establish the relationship; a clear opening gives the topic and purpose. Develop a few connected points using language listeners can follow. Signposts such as first and finally can help without replacing actual reasoning. A conclusion draws the message together and may propose a suitable action. This task prepares the script; a text-only screen cannot assess pace, voice, eye contact or listening response.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to prepare a talk with an appropriate address, clear message, supporting points and a purposeful ending. Builds on: directed writing, letters and argumentative paragraph organisation. Leads to: spoken delivery practice and later reports for different audiences.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: Original model: Fellow learners, our reading room belongs to everyone who uses it. Today I ask us to keep its materials useful. First, return each book to the agreed place so another reader can find it. Next, report damaged materials rather than hiding the problem. Finally, listen when others explain the borrowing arrangements. Small organised actions can make shared reading easier. Let us agree on responsibilities and review how well they work. Thank you.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: State audience, occasion and purpose before drafting. Use examples and direct language suited to listeners. Read the script with a partner or teacher if possible, but do not confuse a completed written task with an assessed oral performance. Preserve factual accuracy even when seeking a memorable phrase.

paper_task.prompt: Write a talk for fellow learners about caring for a shared school resource. Give a suitable address, connected supported points and a purposeful ending. Oral delivery can be practised separately with a teacher.
model: Original model: Fellow learners, our reading room belongs to everyone who uses it. Today I ask us to keep its materials useful. First, return each book to the agreed place so another reader can find it. Next, report damaged materials rather than hiding the problem. Finally, listen when others explain the borrowing arrangements. Small organised actions can make shared reading easier. Let us agree on responsibilities and review how well they work. Thank you.
checklist: My opening fits the audience and purpose.
My points and examples are easy for a listener to follow.
My ending follows the message; I have checked accuracy and grammar.
